data.description:
## Why
An agent that reads a terminal nobody has shown yet gets "Failed to read terminal text" or "Terminal surface not found", even when a send to that same tab would have started it. Backlog item: B087.

## Evidence
origin/main `0ff8887e5e`.

- `send_text` already calls `requestBackgroundSurfaceStartIfNeeded` and waits off main (`Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift:4144`, send path in `SurfaceHandlers` and `TerminalController` near the 2 s wait).
- `v2SurfaceReadText` in `Sources/SocketHandlers/SurfaceHandlers.swift` reads immediately. It does not start the surface and does not wait. The comment above it says the read matches clear-history and has no `waitForTerminalSurface`.
- Upstream cmux #14673 (`bcf012219b`).
- Research: Fable §3 B087 and wave 1. Astra §3. This is the read half of C11-130, C11-169, and C11-235. The stuck bootstrap window (B003) is a different ticket.

## Scope
In: `read_text` and `read-screen` use the same start-and-wait helper `send_text` already uses, off the main actor, with the existing timeout. A never-shown terminal that can be started returns its text. A terminal that cannot be started returns the existing not-ready error after the wait, not immediately.

Out:
- Re-adopting a parked bootstrap window (B003). If the helper returns early because `headlessStartupWindow` is already set, this ticket still times out. That fix is the app ticket.
- Moving scrollback formatting off main (B086). Land this first. The app ticket rebases onto it.
- Failing closed on a stale explicit ref (B066). That rides the app ticket. Do not change the fallback in this PR, or the two PRs will collide. If you must touch the fallback line to call the helper, leave the fallback behavior as it is and say so.
- `read-selection` (C11-282).

## Approach
Call `requestBackgroundSurfaceStartIfNeeded` and the existing off-main wait from the read handler before the main-actor format. Keep the format where it is. The app ticket moves it. Do not add a second waiter and do not pump the main run loop.

## Acceptance criteria
1. On a tagged build, `new-surface` a terminal and `read-screen` it before anyone focuses it. The call returns the shell's text, or the shell prompt, within the same budget `send` uses.
2. `read-screen` on a tab that was just closed still fails. It does not hang past the wait.
3. A focused terminal's `read-screen` still returns the screen it did before this change.

## Validation
`tests_v2` against a tagged socket. No computer-use pass required beyond confirming the new tab is not a sliver if you screenshot it. Builds on Atlas after C11-216. No soak. No source-grep test.

## Dependencies
None inside this workstream. The app-half ticket depends on this one. Cross-workstream: F1 is C11-216 for the tagged build. The lead links it.

## Risks
Main thread: the wait stays off main, same as send. Do not wrap the wait in `v2MainSync`. Doctrine: no tenant config. No new strings. Public repo: a start-and-wait, not a hang recipe.

Size: S. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: reuse the send-path helper. No new lifecycle.

C11-296 implementation handoff

Head: e49dd2754b (full identity from linked branch / PR #511)
Base: 7bb785741750ddeb8ab12b4cf6472593fb8c3550
Draft PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/511
Plan: .lattice/plans/task_01M3X6K1X04S08YS80HNASRCMN.md

Observed checks: `python3 -m py_compile tests_v2/test_read_screen_cold_start.py` passed; `git diff --check` passed. These are syntax/patch checks, not runtime tests. GitHub CI is pending at this comment; owner stays available to repair failures and records the result separately. No local Swift builds, unit runs, operator-session socket tests, or runtime claims.

Host regressions in ColdTerminalReadTests start from a verified absent runtime and check that read demand creates it without selection changes. A second fixture removes the workspace on the ready notification between resolution and final read, retaining the terminal to catch stale-object reads. CI's host suite is advisory, so inspect these individual results rather than treating the overall build gate as proof they passed.

Validator scenario (runtime deferred to batch per go-owner.md; C11-296 is outside the runtime risk list and no typing/input/focus paths changed):
1. Build merged main as a tagged QA app on Atlas, record SHA, socket, load average and unlocked screen. Use the isolated sandbox test route; never the operator session. Run host class c11Tests/ColdTerminalReadTests and require both assertions to pass.
2. Run tests_v2/test_read_screen_cold_start.py through the sandbox runner with its explicit socket and CLI. Before any send/focus, create an unfocused terminal in a background workspace and read its UUID. Expect a successful text payload within the shared two-second readiness budget plus measured scheduling allowance; a blank first payload is allowed before shell output. Poll only reads for the prompt. Expect selected workspace and focused tab unchanged. Record first-read elapsed time.
3. The script focuses the target only after cold-start checks, prints eight synthetic Unicode lines, checks canonical and compatibility reads, text/base64 parity and last-N bounds, then shipped CLI read-screen. Expect the final numbered Unicode line on every path. Existing capture-pane parity scenario may be run as an additional full viewport/scrollback check.
4. Close the exact UUID and read it again. Expect an error within the readiness budget plus 2 seconds scheduling allowance, never another tab's text. The host removal fixture covers a target disappearing after resolution.
5. Repeat the cold-read scenario on a tagged origin/main baseline on the same host; record baseline/candidate timings and host load. No dedicated soak is required. No claim of measured typing latency from the owner.

Cut line: formatting remains on main for C11-295, unresolved explicit fallback is unchanged, B003 bootstrap re-adoption and legacy v1 read_screen are untouched. No new strings or migrations. C11-295 must rebase onto this separate small PR. Skill source changed; only Merge Captain syncs installed copy after merge. Shared upstream incident B087/cmux #14673 already has an upstream fix; this patch reuses c11's own waiter.

# C11-296 review, cycle 1

Verdict: **PASS** for code review at `e49dd2754ba4fa87dae5db591328440d3fcf96f1`.

PR: #511. Base / merge-base with fetched origin/main: `7bb785741750ddeb8ab12b4cf6472593fb8c3550`. The remote PR head and base still match these identities at closeout. Reviewed the entire four-file diff, ticket, stored plan, validation comment, repository policies, philosophy, attention-loop AAR, and the unchanged dispatch, startup, teardown, resolution and capture seams.

This is a static review. No builds, tests or runtime validation were performed by this reviewer. The owner's recorded checks establish Python syntax and patch cleanliness only. Build and compatibility CI remain queued; the Merge Captain must enforce green exact-head CI. Runtime acceptance is explicitly assigned to the batch Validator by the review brief and go-owner.md, so its absence is not a code-review blocker for this ticket.

## Blocking

None found.

`Sources/SocketHandlers/SurfaceHandlers.swift:1179-1225` resolves on main, invokes the existing two-second readiness helper on the socket worker, then checks both workspace membership and terminal identity before fetching the current runtime on main. The returned readiness pointer is never dereferenced off main. Formatting, response fields, resolution fallback and unavailable-runtime error behavior remain compatible with the prior handler; C11-295 can reuse this sequence.

Canonical and compatibility methods reach the worker dispatcher through existing alias normalization (`Sources/SocketHandlers/SocketDispatch.swift:25-69`, `Sources/TerminalController.swift:2084-2088`). Concurrent requests reuse the existing startup guard: request scheduling and creation are serialized on main, `backgroundSurfaceStartQueued` coalesces pending work, and the creation closure checks `surface == nil` again (`Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift:4345-4375`). The hidden-window path contains no window activation or selection call. No telemetry, typing-path, tenant configuration, persistence or localization changes were introduced.

The new host fixtures exercise the actual handler from an absent runtime and remove the workspace during the ready notification while retaining the terminal. They would distinguish missing demand-start and stale-object reads. The socket fixture exercises real output, aliases, Unicode, encoding, CLI capture and a closed UUID; these are behavioral tests rather than source inspections.

## Non-blocking

1. `tests_v2/test_read_screen_cold_start.py:35-46`: the first-read elapsed time is printed without an assertion, and calls use the client's default 20-second timeout. A successful nine-second first read could still produce the script's PASS output. The Validator scenario separately requires checking the recorded elapsed time, so this is an automation gap rather than evidence of a handler defect. Smallest improvement: assert the agreed two-second startup budget plus scheduling allowance on the first call, and make prompt polling share a bounded deadline with per-call timeouts derived from its remaining time. This does not establish a whole-request guarantee for a wedged main queue; that belongs to C11-295.

2. `c11Tests/TerminalAndGhosttyTests.swift:3305` and `tests_v2/test_read_screen_cold_start.py:35`: each fixture issues one cold read. They do not independently measure the brief's concurrent-read, exactly-once requirement. The existing serialized startup guards support it statically. A small additional behavioral check can issue two simultaneous reads of one verified-cold terminal and count one ready notification / one runtime creation, without adding production lifecycle machinery.

## Runtime proof still required

1. **Merge Captain:** require green CI at the reviewed head before landing, and inspect the individual `ColdTerminalReadTests` results. The host-test step is advisory (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:238`), so an overall green build alone does not prove these assertions passed.
2. **Batch Validator on Atlas:** follow the owner's numbered scenario against an isolated tagged QA app and explicit socket/CLI. Record actual SHA, host load and timings. Require both host fixtures to pass, including the absent-runtime precondition and rejection after workspace removal.
3. Before sending or focusing, read the cold terminal's exact UUID, verify startup and eventual real shell output, and compare the first-read timing with the existing two-second readiness budget plus measured scheduling allowance. An initially empty successful payload is permitted before shell output. Confirm selected workspace, focused tab and macOS app focus remain unchanged. Also issue simultaneous cold reads and verify one runtime creation with successful responses for the same UUID.
4. Verify warmed viewport/scrollback and last-N capture, Unicode and text/base64 parity, canonical and compatibility methods, and shipped CLI read-screen. Run the existing capture-pane parity scenario for full viewport/scrollback comparison. Close the UUID and require an error within the stated allowance. Compare candidate and baseline timings on the same host. No runtime success, latency result or completed soak is claimed here.

The owner's scenario can prove the three ticket acceptance criteria when its expected timing is checked explicitly; it needs the concurrent-read observation above to prove the additional focus in the review brief. The batch deferral is authorized. Installed skill synchronization remains the Merge Captain's post-merge responsibility.

Compatibility app build/smoke passed: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/actions/runs/36971736685 . GhosttyKit, workflow guards, web typecheck and remote-daemon tests also passed. - ColdTerminalReadTests.testReadStartsNeverPresentedTerminalWithoutChangingSelection PASSED, 0.110 s.
